drafts.name: bracket-operations-with-explicit-pre-and-post-checks
drafts.description: Every non-trivial operation should be surrounded by two explicit verification gates: (1) a pre-condition gate that confirms all prerequisites actually exist in the current system state before the operation begins, and (2) a post-condition gate that enumerates each intended target or outcome and confirms it was actually achieved. This bracket pattern recurred in three distinct forms across the session: verifying a root cause still holds before applying a fix (pre), ensuring prerequisite data/components are present before running a task that depends on them (pre), and enumerating intended targets after execution and checking each one was processed (post). Neither gate is optional.

drafts.name: enforce-invariants-structurally-not-procedurally
drafts.description: When a correctness constraint can be made structurally unviolable — through data-type design, infrastructure wiring, or explicit enumeration — prefer that over relying on discipline at runtime. This principle surfaced in three distinct forms: encoding co-occurring fields as atomic invariants in state machines so partial/inconsistent state cannot be represented; using real infrastructure so fake or stub paths cannot silently substitute for real ones; and enumerating all intended targets explicitly so coverage gaps are forced to be visible rather than silently absent. In each case, the structural approach eliminates an entire class of silent violation that a procedural check could only catch after the fact.

drafts.name: silent-success-is-not-success
drafts.description: A recurring failure mode across the session: treating the absence of an error signal — zero exit code, no exception thrown, no timeout logged — as positive confirmation that work completed correctly and completely. The pattern surfaced in at least three forms: trusting a zero exit code as proof of full target coverage, trusting that a spawned server task 'ran' because no error appeared, and trusting that an aged diagnosis still matches the current root cause. The correct posture is that absence of error is neutral; positive confirmation requires an explicit, observable outcome for each intended target.

drafts.description: When the system has a correctness requirement — co-occurring fields, a real infrastructure dependency, a server that must be actively running before requests arrive — enforce it through explicit, mechanical means (code assertions, required config, active polling, concrete wiring). Never rely on convention, documentation, naming, or assumed ambient behavior to maintain the invariant; implicit reliance silently fails.

drafts.name: Treat tasks as atomic — prerequisite-first, enumerated, completed
drafts.description: Tasks must be treated as atomic units with three properties: (1) all prerequisite artefacts and conditions are confirmed in place before execution begins, (2) every intended target is explicitly enumerated up front and verified afterward, and (3) the task is driven all the way to verified completion without pausing unnecessarily mid-stream. Partial execution, assumed completion, or mid-task confirmation pauses all introduce the same failure mode: work that appears done but isn't.

drafts.name: Verify actual current state before acting
drafts.description: Before taking any consequential action — applying a fix, assuming a process completed, or relying on a prior assumption — always verify the actual current state of the system. Do not assume that expected conditions still hold, that a prior step succeeded silently, or that historical context (aged todos, prior runs) reflects today's reality.

The overarching rule: the user owns the workflow rhythm; the agent owns individual task execution.

drafts.name: Restrained autonomous orchestration — defer sequencing and chaining to the user

Both the decision to run tasks in parallel (checking for shared state first) and the decision to trigger downstream steps (e.g. review after ticket work) must either follow an explicit user preference or be held for user approval. Default to the most conservative, least-surprising posture: sequential, and stop at the natural end of the requested scope.

drafts.name: comprehension-before-commitment
drafts.description: Before writing any code or making any architectural decision, build a complete mental model of the system: read all versioned plans up to the current version, trace every relevant logic path, identify all component interfaces, and understand how every piece fits together. Commitment (writing code, opening PRs, merging) on partial context produces implementations that violate existing contracts, miss edge cases, or duplicate logic already handled elsewhere.

drafts.name: full-fidelity-in-both-understanding-and-validation
drafts.description: Shortcuts in comprehension and shortcuts in validation produce the same failure mode: the system appears correct while a real violation goes undetected. Full-fidelity understanding (read all plans, trace all paths, understand all interfaces) and full-fidelity validation (assert on real content, validate all coupled layers) are two expressions of a single discipline: never accept a partial view as a complete one. Gaps in either phase are silent — they feel like green until the production failure reveals them.

drafts.name: proxy-metric-validation-antipattern
drafts.description: Using indirect signals — version counters, single-layer checks, surface-level status codes — as stand-ins for real correctness validation produces false greens. The proxy can succeed while the underlying invariant silently fails. Validation must always target the actual invariant directly: real content retrievability, all coupled layers agreeing, the substantive outcome — not a metric that merely correlates with it.

drafts.name: Before working on any feature or fix, read (preference)
drafts.description: Standing user preference: Before working on any feature or fix, read all implementation plans up to the current version, walk every logic path, inspect every interface, and understand the full codebase rather than reasoning from a partial view.

drafts.name: Complete Context is a Hard Prerequisite Before Any Action
drafts.description: Skills 2 and 3 converge on a single meta-rule: the agent must hold complete context before it is permitted to act. Skill 3 requires reading every implementation plan up to the current version, walking every logic path, and inspecting every interface. Skill 2 requires treating the full system context as the active dynamic layer for all decisions. Together they assert that partial context — knowing only the immediate file, only the current plan, or only the runtime state — is categorically insufficient and will lead to decisions that are locally sensible but globally broken. The session-spanning principle is: completeness of understanding is a non-negotiable gate, not an optimization.

drafts.name: In tests, always assert on the retrieved content (preference)
drafts.description: Standing user preference: In tests, always assert on the retrieved content itself — asserting only that a version number bumped is a false green when retrieval status is degraded; content retrievability must be verified directly.

drafts.name: Never Accept a Proxy Signal as Proof of the Real Invariant
drafts.description: Two distinct skills share the same underlying failure mode: accepting a correlated side-effect or surrogate signal as evidence that the real invariant holds. Skill 1 warns that updating one coupled layer while leaving others untouched creates a false sense of consistency. Skill 4 warns that asserting a version bump instead of asserting the retrieved content itself creates a false green in tests. Both are instances of proxy verification — checking something adjacent to the actual condition rather than the condition itself. The session-spanning lesson is: always verify the primary invariant directly; never let a correlated proxy stand in for the real check.

drafts.name: Operate as an autonomous coding harness agent, using (preference)
drafts.description: Standing user preference: Operate as an autonomous coding harness agent, using the provided system context as the active dynamic layer for all decisions and actions.

drafts.name: Partial Compliance Equals Non-Compliance
drafts.description: Skills 1, 3, and 4 each instantiate the same high-altitude rule in a different engineering phase: partial adherence to a requirement is treated as a failure, not a partial success. In implementation (skill 1), updating one coupled layer while leaving others unchanged violates the invariant just as completely as updating none. In pre-work preparation (skill 3), reading some plans or some paths is not better-than-nothing — the missed paths are exactly where bugs hide. In testing (skill 4), asserting one observable proxy when the full content must be verified gives the same false confidence as no assertion. The session-spanning principle: wherever a completeness requirement exists, there is no partial credit — you are either complete or you are wrong.
